text_blocks.snippet: Shingles, also known as herpes zoster, typically presents with a painful rash, often on one side of the body or face. The rash is characterized by blisters that may break open and scab over. Before the rash appears, individuals may experience pain, tingling, or burning sensations in the area where the rash will develop. Other symptoms can include fever, headache, chills, and upset stomach.
snippet_highlighted_words: a painful rash, often on one side of the body or face

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed breakdown of shingles symptoms:

list.snippet: Pain, tingling, or burning: This is often the first sign, occurring on one side of the body or face.
Skin sensitivity: The affected area may be sensitive to touch or even clothing.
Flu-like symptoms: Some people experience fatigue, headache, or mild fever.
Red patches: These appear on the skin, usually in a band-like pattern on one side of the body.
Blisters: Small, fluid-filled blisters develop within a few days.
